content.overview: BNS s. 148 — Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147. BNS restatement of IPC 121A. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 121A. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 148 is the rule on “Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147”. The section provides that whoever within or without and beyond India conspires to commit any of the offences punishable by section 147, or conspires to overawe, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, the Central Government or any State Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 148 exists so that “Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147” has a closed legal test in Chapter VII — Of Offences Against the State. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Waging war, and the new s. 152 on sovereignty, unity and integrity — not a relabel of sedition.

The provision in detail
148. Whoever within or without and beyond India conspires to commit any of the offences punishable by section 147, or conspires to overawe, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, the Central Government or any State Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever within or without and beyond India conspires to commit any of the offences punishable by section 147, or conspires to overawe, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, the Central Government or any State Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Explanations
Explanation.—To constitute a conspiracy under this section, it is not necessary that any act or illegal omission shall take place in pursuance thereof

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 148 (Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 148 (Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 147), Chapter VII — Of Offences Against the State.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever within or without and beyond India conspires to commit any of the offences punishable by section 147, or conspires to overawe, by means of criminal force or the show of criminal force, the Central Government or any State Government, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 148 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
